segments.text: Welcome back. Today we are going to talk about risk assessment and why it matters for security teams.
Risk assessment is the process of identifying, analyzing and evaluating risk against a set of objectives.
Let me define the three components clearly. Risk is the combination of likelihood and impact.
Asset identification comes first. You cannot protect what you have not written down.
In one study we ran last year, teams that documented assets recovered forty percent faster after an incident.
Threat identification follows. That is where you list what could go wrong against those assets.
To be precise: risk assessment identifies potential threats, evaluates their likelihood, and evaluates their potential impact.
Risk assessment evaluates the likelihood of a threat materialising. Likelihood is usually rated low, medium or high.
Impact is rated the same way, and the two ratings are multiplied to produce a risk score.
Remember the core definition: risk assessment is the process of identifying, analyzing and evaluating risk against a set of objectives.
The four standard treatment options are mitigation, transfer, acceptance and avoidance.
That is the core of the framework. Next time we will walk through mitigation in detail.
